title: Engine will not start
shortDescription: Engine cranks but does not fire.
fullDescription:
Simplicity tractors with B&S or Kohler engines suffer the typical stale-fuel and clogged-carb issues after winter storage.

Fresh fuel, new plug, and a carb cleaning resolve most cases.

fixSteps.title: Fresh fuel & plug
fixSteps.instruction: Drain old gas, install fresh, replace plug.

title: Mower deck PTO will not engage
shortDescription: PTO switch does nothing when pulled.
fullDescription:
Simplicity uses electric PTO clutches. Failure to engage is usually a blown fuse or seat switch issue.

Older Broadmoors with mechanical PTO levers can have a stretched cable or frozen clutch.

faq.a: Yes but at half throttle is preferred.

title: Hydrostatic transmission noisy
fullDescription:
Simplicity uses Tuff Torq hydrostatic transmissions on most models. Noise indicates aerated fluid or low fluid level.

Purging and a fluid change usually resolve it.

fixSteps.title: Purge
fixSteps.instruction: Push forward and reverse 5x with bypass open.

fixSteps.title: Change fluid
fixSteps.instruction: Drain and refill with Tuff Torq fluid.

title: Mower cuts uneven
shortDescription: Stripes show one side cuts shorter.
fullDescription: Simplicity's free-floating deck still requires periodic leveling. Tire pressure and bent blades are the next checks.

fixSteps.title: Verify tire pressures
fixSteps.instruction: Check both rear tires equal pressure.

fixSteps.title: Level deck
fixSteps.instruction: Adjust deck rods to equal blade tip height.

faq.a: Blade tip to floor at 3 and 9 o'clock.

title: Deck belt thrown
shortDescription: Belt falls off pulleys during use.
fullDescription: Worn idler bearings, weak tensioner spring, or stretched belt cause belts to throw. Inspect entire belt path and replace any worn idler.

fixSteps.title: Replace components
fixSteps.instruction: Swap belt and any rough idlers.

title: Engine will not crank
fullDescription: Battery, cables, solenoid, or interlocks are the suspects.

title: Steering wheel has excessive play
shortDescription: Wheel turns 30 degrees before tires move.
fullDescription:
Simplicity steering uses sector and pinion gears that wear over time. Backlash above 1 inch at the wheel rim warrants inspection.

Loose tie-rod ends and worn axle bushings also contribute.

fixSteps.title: Inspect tie rods
fixSteps.instruction: Check for play at each end with mower jacked up.

title: Engine overheats
fullDescription: Air-cooled engines need clean cooling fins. Grass packed in the shroud is the leading cause.

fixSteps.title: Clean fins
fixSteps.instruction: Remove shroud and brush all debris.

title: Fuel leaking
shortDescription: Gasoline drips from carb or fuel line.
fullDescription: Stuck float, deteriorated fuel lines from ethanol exposure, or a cracked carb bowl — all common after long storage.

title: Poor grass discharge
shortDescription: Clippings clump or build up under deck.
fullDescription: Dull blades, slow ground speed, or wet grass cause poor discharge. Sharpen blades, clean underside of deck, mow when dry.

fixSteps.title: Sharpen blades
fixSteps.instruction: Remove and sharpen to factory edge.
